opførsel.explanation: "Opførsel" means "behavior". To say someone behaves badly, use "dårlig opførsel" (bad behavior): "Dårlig opførsel er ikke tilladt" (Bad behavior is not allowed). To talk about manners, use "manerer" (manners): "gode manerer" (good manners).

ophidset.explanation: "Ophidset" means "agitated". To describe a heated argument, use it before the noun: "en ophidset debat" (a heated debate). It can also mean sexually aroused.

opkast.explanation: "Opkast" means "vomit". It is built from "op" (up) and "et kast" (a throw), like the verb "at kaste op" (to throw up). To say a child is throwing up, use the verb: "Barnet kaster op" (The child is throwing up).

opladning.explanation: "Opladning" means "charging". It comes from the verb "at oplade" (to charge). To say you charge a phone, use the verb: "Jeg lader telefonen op" (I am charging the phone).

oplagt.explanation: "Oplagt" means "obvious". When you describe a person who is full of energy, it also means "in good form": "Hun er godt oplagt i dag" (She is in good form today).

opmærksom.explanation: "Opmærksom" means "attentive". To say you are aware of something, add "på" (on) after it: "Jeg er opmærksom på problemet" (I am aware of the problem).

opmærksom på.explanation: "Opmærksom på" means "aware of". To point something out to someone, use "at gøre nogen opmærksom på" (to make someone aware of): "Jeg gjorde ham opmærksom på fejlen" (I pointed out the mistake to him).

opmærksomhed.explanation: "Opmærksomhed" means "attention". It is the noun for the word "opmærksom" (attentive). To ask a room for its attention, say: "Må jeg bede om jeres opmærksomhed?" (May I have your attention?)

oppe.explanation: "Oppe" means "up". When something is already in a high place, use it: "Katten er oppe på bordet" (The cat is up on the table). When something moves up, use "op" (up) instead: "Katten hopper op på bordet" (The cat jumps up onto the table). To ask whether someone is out of bed, use it too: "Er du oppe?" (Are you up?)

oprevet.explanation: "Oprevet" means "upset". To say someone is upset after something unpleasant, use it with "efter" (after): "Hun var meget oprevet efter skænderiet" (She was very upset after the argument).

oprigtig.explanation: "Oprigtig" means "sincere". To give your honest opinion, use it before the noun: "Det er min oprigtige mening" (That is my sincere opinion). To tell someone to speak the truth, use "ærlig" (honest) instead: "Vær ærlig" (Be honest).

oprindelig.explanation: "Oprindelig" means "original". For something new and creative, use "original" instead: "en original idé" (an original idea). To say what was true at the start, use "oprindeligt" (originally): "Oprindeligt boede vi i Aarhus" (Originally we lived in Aarhus).

oprørsk.explanation: "Oprørsk" means "rebellious". It comes from the noun "et oprør" (a revolt). To describe a teenager who refuses to follow the rules: "en oprørsk teenager" (a rebellious teenager).

oprørt.explanation: "Oprørt" means "upset". It can also describe water: "et oprørt hav" (a rough sea). To say what upset someone, use "over" (about): "oprørt over nyheden" (upset about the news).

opsyn.explanation: "Opsyn" means "supervision". To say who is being watched over, use it with "under" (under): "Børnene er under opsyn" (The children are being supervised).

optaget.explanation: "Optaget" means "busy". When a seat or a table is in use, it means "taken": "Er denne plads optaget?" (Is this seat taken?) When a person has no time, it means "busy": "Jeg er optaget lige nu" (I am busy right now).

optimistisk.explanation: "Optimistisk" means "optimistic". It is the adjective for the noun "en optimist" (an optimist). To say you are cautiously optimistic: "Jeg er forsigtigt optimistisk" (I am cautiously optimistic).

opvaskemiddel.explanation: "Opvaskemiddel" means "dish soap". It is built from "at vaske op" (to wash dishes) and "et middel" (a product). For clothes, use "vaskepulver" (laundry detergent) instead: "Jeg køber vaskepulver" (I buy laundry detergent).

orange.explanation: "Orange" means "orange", as in the color. For the fruit, use "en appelsin" (an orange): "Jeg spiser en appelsin" (I am eating an orange).

ordblind.explanation: "Ordblind" means "dyslexic". It is built from "ord" (word) and "blind" (blind), so it is literally "word-blind".

ordentlig.explanation: "Ordentlig" means "proper". When you describe a person, it means "decent": "en ordentlig mand" (a decent man). To say how something is done, use "ordentligt" (properly): "Gør det ordentligt" (Do it properly).

organiseret.explanation: "Organiseret" means "organized". It comes from the verb "at organisere" (to organize). To say something is well organized, add "vel" (well) in front: "velorganiseret" (well organized).

original.explanation: "Original" means "original", as in the first version rather than a copy. For a creative, new idea, it has a second meaning: "en original idé" (an original idea).

os.explanation: "Os" means "us". When someone sees or helps us, use it: "Han ser os" (He sees us). When we are the ones doing the action, use "vi" (we): "Vi ser ham" (We see him).

ost.explanation: "Ost" means "cheese". To talk about one kind of cheese, put "en" before it: "en fransk ost" (a French cheese).
